2027 Volkswagen T-Roc R Performance Crossover Gets Teased With Series-Production Everything
17 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
The largest European automaker of them all has recently published official spy photos of the upcoming T-Roc R, showcasing a prototype loaded with series-production body panels and trim pieces. Its rear end tells us quite a bit about the direction of this crossover, starting with the quad exhaust outlets and sporty-looking aerodynamic diffuser.
Equipped with front and rear light bars connecting the headlight and taillight clusters, the 2027 model further prides itself on illuminated VW badging. Performance-oriented wheels and larger brakes can also be seen, whereas the front bumper gets its own aggressive treatment, separating the performance version from lesser T-Roc trim levels.
Disguised under blue-and-white camo wrap, the next-generation Volkswagen T-Roc R also benefits from larger front bumper openings. Not only does it have different cooling requirements due to its 2.0-liter turbo iron-block gasoline mill, but a performance-oriented crossover also has to cool its front brakes properly.
Its four tailpipes are particularly interesting, with Volkswagen using quad pipes to distinguish full-on R models from the regular trim level range. Circular tips are on the menu, and there is a slim chance that Volkswagen will offer an optional Akrapovic performance exhaust setup. In the previous generation's case, the Akrapovic unit was manufactured exclusively from high-grade titanium alloy.
Lighter than the stock stainless-steel system, the Akrapovic exhaust also makes sense when you remember that its compact hatchback and wagon siblings can also be had with titanium systems. The axle-back exhaust of the Golf R sheds roughly 7 kilograms (15 pounds) compared to the stainless-steel arrangement.
Photo: Volkswagen A different muffler also makes it stand out in the crowd. Titanium has different acoustic properties compared to stainless steel, and the resulting thinner walls resonate differently as well, giving the exhaust a crisper and higher-pitched edge under load. Slightly louder overrun crackles are part of its appeal as well.
Rolling on 20-inch forged alloys, the pictured test vehicle builds on the T-Roc R-Line's styling with more pronounced elements up front and for the rear end. As per Volkswagen's technical documentation for the second-generation T-Roc, a high-output 2.0 TSI with mild-hybrid assistance is planned for the compact-sized crossover, and the only application we can think of is the new T-Roc R.
In eTSI flavor, it's easy to imagine over 300 horsepower and more than 300 pound-feet of twist on premium unleaded. It remains to be seen, however, if the Wolfsburg-based manufacturer's R division will match or exceed the current Golf R's 328 horsepower and 310 pound-feet (420 Newton-meters). Neither the hatchback nor the wagon comes with a 48-volt system as of this writing.
Certain to feature the seven-speed DSG with wet clutches, the T-Roc R is a genuinely interesting thriller when you remember that Volkswagen is certain to use 4MOTION with R Performance Torque Vectoring. That's another way of saying two independently controlled multi-plate clutches for the rear axle. Similar to standard 4MOTION, this system also distributes up to 50 percent of the available torque to the rear wheels.
R Performance Torque Vectoring indicates that all of the torque going to the rear axle can be sent to either rear wheel, helping the T-Roc R rotate better while cornering to reduce understeer, thus helping the driver accelerate out of the corner faster. R Performance Torque Vectoring also features a Drift Mode on the Golf R, and this mode is certain to carry over to the T-Roc R as well.
According to Volkswagen's November 2025 fact sheet about the second-generation T-Roc , the R will be unleashed at the beginning of 2027. With a bit of luck, the first units will be delivered in the summer of 2027.
